title: US States Take on Meta in Landmark Trial
paragraphs: Four US states have taken Meta, the owner of Facebook and Instagram, to trial in what is being described as the biggest legal fight yet over the harm social media may cause to children.

The trial began on August 18 in federal court in Oakland, California. The four states, California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey, are among the dozens of states that sued Meta three years ago over child safety and privacy. The remaining states are expected to have their cases heard later. Jurors will give an advisory verdict, but the final decision on whether Meta is responsible will be made by US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers.

The states accuse Meta of deliberately designing features that make its platforms addictive for children, contributing to a mental health crisis among young people. According to the lawsuit, Meta has used "powerful and unprecedented technologies to entice, engage, and ultimately ensnare youth and teens." The states argue that keeping children on its platforms for longer increased Meta's revenue. They also accuse the company of collecting data from children under the age of 13 without their parents' permission, which they say breaks federal law.

The stakes are enormous. According to a legal filing by Meta, the maximum possible penalties could theoretically reach around $1.4 trillion. However, legal experts say a penalty anywhere near that amount is extremely unlikely. James Grimmelmann, a law professor at Cornell University, said an award that large would put Meta into bankruptcy. The states are also seeking changes to the way Facebook and Instagram operate.

Meta denies the accusations. The company says the evidence will show its commitment to young people, and it argues that the proposed penalty has no connection to any actual violation. It points to safety features such as Instagram's teen accounts, introduced in 2024, which include private settings by default, content restrictions and parental controls.

The case comes after a difficult year for Meta in court. Earlier this year, a jury in Los Angeles awarded $6 million to a young woman who said she became addicted to social media as a child. In addition, a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to introduce new safety measures for young users in that state, including time limits.
